lines.li: [them] Has your colony thought about what it will ask of us?
[us] Not yet, there's been no need.
[them,their:lowtech] Then let it keep, a debt like ours doesn't spoil.
[them] Good, I'd rather it was something worth the asking.
[us] What we did for your people wasn't much.
[them] It was {FAVOURWHY}, and it was a great deal to us.
[us,trait:Kind] Anyone would have done it.
[us] Then I'm glad it helped.
[them] Plenty of people could have done it, and you're the ones who did.
[them] Our children are taught the names of every people we owe a gift to.
[us] Is our colony one of them?
[them] It is, and they say it better than I do.
[them] The reeve had it cried in the market that our town owes yours.
[us] For {FAVOURWHY}?
[them] For that, and loud enough that the fishwives can tell you the whole story.
[them] Our quartermaster keeps two columns, what we owe and what we're owed.
[us] And we're in the first one.
[them] Near the top of it, for {FAVOURWHY}.
[us] Leave us there a while, we're in no hurry.
[them] Your colony's entry is still flagged open in our records.
[us] Does that bother anyone?
[them] Open entries bother everyone where I come from, so ask when you're ready.
[them] At court an unpaid favor is mentioned at every dinner until it is repaid.
[us] That sounds tiresome for you.
[them] It is, so I would take it kindly if your colony asked for something soon.
[them] I'm only here to trade, but even I know my people owe yours.
[us] Do they say what for?
[them] For {FAVOURWHY}, and they say it often.
[them] Your stores look thin, and my people owe your colony.
[us] Are you offering?
[them] It isn't mine to give, but a load of food is a fair thing to call the debt in for.
[them] When I heard raiders had come at you, I thought you'd call the debt in.
[us] Not for that, not this time.
[them] Then keep it for a worse day, I hope it never comes.
[them] We owe your colony, and we'll pay it, but don't make a long list.
[us] One thing, when we need it.
[them] One thing, then.
[them] My people owe yours, which is the only reason I'm being civil.
[us] Then I'll take the civility and say thank you.
[them] I'd rather owe your colony than any people I know.
[us] That's a strange kind of compliment.
[them,their:lowtech] Among my people it is the best kind, it means we trust you to ask fairly.
[them] Where I come from it's a good one, it means we trust you to ask fairly.
[us] Then we'll try to deserve it.
[them] At home your name comes up whenever someone mentions {FAVOURWHY}.
[us] Kindly, I hope.
[them] Kindly, and with the reminder that one of ours owes you for it.
[them] You know there's a favor owed to you among my people?
[us,trait:Kind] I didn't help them to be owed anything.
[us] I'd heard something like it.
[them] Why you did it doesn't matter much, it's owed all the same.
[us] Then I'll remember it, if I'm ever in a corner.
[them] Among my people the one who owes you would make you a gift with their own hands.
[us] They don't need to.
[them] They do, or the debt sits on them like a stone in a boot.
[them] A favor owed to you in person binds harder than one owed to a town.
[us] I never asked anyone to bind themselves to me.
[them] You didn't have to ask, that's how it works with us.
[them] Somebody at home owes you personally, and keeps reminding the rest of us.
[us] That's kind of them.
[them] It's tiresome, but yes, it's kind.
[us] Is there anything your people need from us?
[them,town:short:food] Food is short at {TOWN} this season, so there may be soon.
[them,town:short:medicine] There's sickness at {TOWN} and too little medicine, so there may be soon.
[them] Not now, and we'll say so when there is.
[us] We'll be ready when you do.
[them] The elders keep what other peoples owe us as knots on a cord.
[us] How many knots for us?
[them] One, but it's tied tight.
[them] My lord keeps your colony's debt in mind and says nothing of it.
[us] We'd rather hear it said than guess at it.
[them] Then hear it: it's owed, and one day it will be asked for.
[them] Your colony is still in our books, for {FAVOURWHY}.
[us] We know, and we mean to pay it.
[them] Good, the bookkeepers like a column that balances.
[them] Our records show an obligation from your colony, for {FAVOURWHY}.
[us] We don't dispute it.
[them] Nobody disputes it until it's called in.
[them] My house remembers what it gave your colony.
[us] So do we.
[them] Good, at court that courtesy is expected of anyone in our debt.
[them] Our fighters came when your colony called for them.
[us] They did, and we owe your people for it.
[them] They'd come again, as long as the debt runs both ways.
[us] Your people helped us when we had nobody else.
[them] That's what neighbors are for.
[us] All the same, we owe you, and we'll pay it.
[them] I know you will, that's why I'm not worried.
[them] Your colony took our help readily enough.
[us] And we'll repay it just as readily.
[them] I hear your colony has called in what my people owe.
[us] We have, and we hope they'll answer.
[them,tone:warm] They will, I'd stake my own name on it.
[them,their:tribal] The elders will talk it over at the fire, and then they'll answer.
[them] They'll answer one way or the other, they always do.
[them] Our council's been arguing about your colony's call since it came in.
[us] Arguing for or against?
[them] About how to pay it, mostly, which I'd take as a good sign.
[them] My people have asked your colony to pay what it owes.
[us] We know, and the council is on it.
[them,town:short:food|town:short:medicine] They need it, I wouldn't ask otherwise.
[them] Then I'll tell them it's in hand.
[them] Your colony kept its word to my people, and it's still talked about at home.
[us] We'd be ashamed to have done otherwise.
[them,their:tribal] Then you think as we do, and that is rare in outsiders.
[them,their:medieval] Then you'd make good neighbors to any honest town.
[them] Plenty of people would have found an excuse.
[them] Since your colony kept its word, my people take yours on trust.
[us] That's worth more to us than silver.
[them] It should be, it's harder to come by.
[them] When my people needed your colony, it found reasons to say no.
[us] We had our own troubles that season.
[us] I know we turned your people away when they called on us.
[them] You did, and it was a long season after.
[us] If they ask again, I'd like the answer to be different.
[them] So would I, so make sure it is.
[them] My people went back on their word to your colony once.
[us] We remember it.
[them,their:lowtech] Some of us carry it like a shame, if that's any use to you.
[them] Some of us are still embarrassed by it, if that helps.
[us] It helps to hear it said.
[us] Your people's word didn't hold the last time we leaned on it.
[them] And you've never once let anyone down, I suppose.
[them] Not everyone of ours came home from the fight at your colony.
[us] We know, and we remember them.
[them,their:tribal] Their names are sung at our fire, and yours with them.
[them,their:medieval] Their families were told they fell keeping an oath, which is some comfort.
[them] Their families know what they died for, and they don't blame you for it.
